historical_claims.anchor: Some wood-decay fungi perform what is called white rot, with enzyme systems capable of substantial lignin modification or mineralization alongside breakdown of other wall material.
In a major comparative-genomics study published in 2012, Dimitrios Floudas and colleagues examined fungal genomes and reconstructed the history of enzymes associated with lignin decay.
E. Toby Kiers and collaborators tested aspects of that exchange experimentally.
In natural conditions, many orchid seeds depend on fungal partners to acquire carbon and other resources needed for germination and early development.
In 2016, Toby Spribille and colleagues reported basidiomycete yeasts embedded in the outer layers of numerous lichens, alongside the better-known fungal and photosynthetic partners.
A large global assessment published in 2019 associated the fungal panzootic with severe declines across hundreds of amphibian species.
Experiments have shown species-specific patterns of manipulation.

A 2017 microscopy study of one ant-fungus pair found fungal cells extensively distributed through the host's body and invading muscle tissue, while not finding them inside the brain at the examined stage.

description: Explores fungal hyphae, wood decay, nutrient exchange with roots, orchid and lichen partnerships, and pathogens, distinguishing observed mechanisms from claims about universal fungal cooperation.
